groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina; to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA); and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Because this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before a meal with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation, analgesic, anti-inflammatory medicine or antirheumatic medicine; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at 15 mg or more a week (15 mg/week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy. In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; impaired cardiovascular circulation (renovascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); liver impairment; impaired heart function; bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or Reye's syndrome; if the user is 14 years of age or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because of the risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are having surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of the tablet.

Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or salicylate preparations, or with methotrexate at 15 mg or more a week (15 mg/week), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline. Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a thrombolytic, another antiplatelet medicine, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), a thiazide diuretic, a lithium preparation, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparation (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with alkaline preparations (for example sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture. Taken together with alcohol it increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (for example difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria); an asthma attack; hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance and, occasionally, rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis); rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, excitement, liver impairment; very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive lowering of body temperature, collapse or coldness of the arms and legs. Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inhibition of blood clot formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, after CABG or PTCA, and reduction of cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Capsule (101804ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For an acute condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, those aged 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, if the user is a baby under 2 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If it is taken together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), tachycardia or high blood pressure occurs, or, very rarely, anaphylaxis, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Difficulty bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis

groups.title: Oral Solution (A49300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 10 to 30 mL in 1 day, divided into doses taken between meals. Dilute 10 mL of this medicine in about half a cup of water and take it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney disease, or if you have or have had myocardial infarction.

This medicine cannot be used as an antidote for alcohol poisoning.

If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection.

If an adverse reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (130501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin, and, together with a hydrocortisone preparation for external use, for eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 6 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime. For people who are sensitive to adverse reactions, take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) per dose, divided into a morning and an evening dose, that is 2 doses. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the interval between doses must be adjusted according to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually taking account of renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if the user is a young child under 6 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia and the like).

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally malaise, numbness, weakness, agitation, abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary lassitude, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, dyskinesia, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, amnesia, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation, nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, cheilitis, taste disturbance, increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia, raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations, vasculitis; occasionally leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, eosinophilia; rarely monocytosis, thrombocytosis, thrombocytopenia, photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching, rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of visual accommodation, oculogyric crisis, vertigo; occasionally liver function disorder with raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, glycosuria, blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting, urinary retention, joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain. After stopping this medicine, itching and urticaria may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, itching of the skin, and eczema and dermatitis when used with a hydrocortisone preparation for external use

groups.title: Tablet (172806ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Ages 11 to 14 years: 200 to 250 mg per dose; ages 7 to 10 years: 150 to 200 mg per dose; ages 3 to 6 years: 100 to 150 mg per dose; ages 1 to 2 years: 50 to 100 mg per dose, taken by mouth 3 to 4 times in 1 day. In children weighing less than 30 kg the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If an increased risk of myocardial infarction or stroke, or serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration or perforation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, reduced granulocytes, leukocytes or platelets, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); raised blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, peripheral oedema, or Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (139503ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of eczema and acne, and as adjunctive treatment of disorders of keratinised areas such as fingernails, toenails or hair that split easily.
groups.usage: Take 2 to 4 capsules (1000 to 2000 mg) in 1 day, for 10 to 20 days in 1 month.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have severe kidney dysfunction or hepatic coma, if the user is a child aged 6 years or younger, or if you have cystinuria.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or if you have kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, occasionally, nausea or, rarely, diarrhoea, thirst or mild abdominal pain occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after meals, during pregnancy, or when it accompanies reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 to 20 mL per dose, 4 times in 1 day (after meals and before bedtime).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you must strictly limit sodium, as in congestive heart failure or kidney impairment; if you have hypercalcaemia, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 7 days of treatment, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If it is taken together with tetracycline, digoxin, a fluoroquinolone, an iron salt, ketoconazole, a neuroleptic, thyroxine, penicillamine, a beta blocker (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), a glucocorticoid, chloroquine, estramustine or a diphosphonate, leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchoconstriction or an anaphylactic reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet per dose: adults (aged 15 years and older) 3 times in 1 day; ages 11 years to under 15 years 2 times in 1 day, before a meal, between meals or after a meal. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), if you have intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 2 times in 1 day, when pain or an attack occurs.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; or if the user is a baby, young child or child (14 years of age or younger) with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver, kidney or thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak; if you have a high fever; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after several doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash and reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite or dizziness occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer, or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking a cough medicine.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema and eczema may occur.

groups.title: Oral Solution (A49300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 10 to 30 mL in 1 day, divided into doses taken between meals. Dilute 10 mL of this medicine in about half a cup of water and take it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney disease, or if you have or have had myocardial infarction.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to caramel.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection. Do not use it as an antidote for alcohol poisoning. If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during previous treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure, high blood pressure or a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; or if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, or high-dose methotrexate used as cancer treatment (15 mg a week or more). Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or low-dose aspirin taken to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (292800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: take 1 tablet per dose. Take it 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime. For the first dose take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like); if you have intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel); if you have severe abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting; if you have a water and electrolyte imbalance (severe dehydration); or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablets; take them with a suitable amount of water.

Do not take it together with an antacid or mineral oil, and do not take it within 1 hour after drinking milk. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a diuretic, an adrenocortical hormone preparation or another laxative.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, cramps, an anaphylactic reaction, angioedema, a hypersensitivity reaction, dehydration, abdominal cramps, nausea, bloody stools, discomfort of the rectum and anus, colitis (including ischaemic colitis), dizziness or fainting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Solution (A74603ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive therapy for symptoms of mental and physical asthenia (weakness).
groups.usage: Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1.0 g per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. Ages 12 to 18 years: take 1.0 g per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, before meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe impairment of kidney or liver function, or myocardial infarction now or in the past.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a problem with urinary retention; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you will take it continuously for 15 days or more; or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an antipsychotic medicine or a sleeping medicine.

If an allergic reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (187501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for its antacid action and for the improvement of symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for constipation.
groups.usage: For gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid: take 2 to 4 tablets (0.5 to 1 g as magnesium oxide) in 1 day, divided into several doses. For constipation: take 8 tablets (2 g) in 1 day, divided into 1 to 2 doses. For the first dose take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney impairment or diarrhoea.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart function or hypermagnesaemia, or if you are an older person (aged 65 years and older).

Because the adsorbent action of this medicine or the rise in the pH of the fluid in the digestive tract may affect the absorption and excretion of medicines taken with it, it must be given with care.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a large amount of milk or with calcium preparations.

If dizziness on standing up, slowing of the pulse, strong drowsiness, clouding of consciousness, a feeling of suffocation, muscle weakness, dry mouth or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Symptoms of magnesium poisoning and, occasionally, diarrhoea may occur.
